author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
Joshua Cooper Ramo is chairman and CEO of Sornay, an investment and advisory firm. Previously he was CEO of Kissinger Associates. Ramo is the author of the new book Darwin’s Lock: America, China and the Shared Future of Nations. His 2004 analysis of “the Beijing consensus” contrasted the Western and Chinese economic development models. He is the author of two New York Times best-selling books and now lives in Shanghai with his family.
For other interviews in the Open Questions series, click...
title: Joshua Cooper Ramo on whether the US can handle the stress test of China’s rise

author: Xinlu Liang
description:
China’s ruling Communist Party will step up “party building” across the country’s tech sector and deploy digital tools to fight corruption, according to a landmark document adopted at a key political plenum.
These tools include a digital discipline inspection platform and a big-data supervision platform. The party will also crack down on corruption involving the internet, virtual currency, cross-border funds and blockchain technology, according to the document formally approved on Thursday at...
title: Communist Party pledges to reach deeper into China’s tech, digital platform sectors

author: Orange Wang
description:
A potential lame-duck phase may not deter US President Donald Trump from pursuing more “transactional” or “risky” foreign policy moves after the midterm elections, Chinese experts warn, while casting doubt on expectations of a powerful Democratic wave.
Amid a season of high-stakes contests that could reshape global politics, the US vote on Tuesday stands out.
The election, which will determine who takes control of the US Congress, could result in Trump and his fellow Republicans no longer...
title: Could a midterm defeat tame Trump? Not on foreign policy, Chinese experts say

author: Carol Yang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has mounted a direct defence of the campaign for strong Communist Party governance and internal discipline, describing them as a “fundamental guarantee” for China’s rise and warning against any easing of scrutiny, according to state media.
Xi took the floor as the party’s 20th Central Committee closed its fifth plenum on Thursday, to directly address the scepticism over the sweeping campaign, state news agency Xinhua reported on Sunday.
According to “side notes”...
title: China’s Xi says strict party governance has positive impact, does not stifle growth

author: Nayan Seth
description:
US first lady Melania Trump is unlikely to travel to China with the president for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen this month.
“First lady Melania Trump is not scheduled to attend the events in person,” her office said in response to a query about her travel plans.
President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit the Philippines for this year’s Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit before travelling to the November 18-19 Apec event, where he will meet his Chinese...
title: US first lady Melania Trump unlikely to travel to Apec summit in China

author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
For decades, China has supplied African militaries with small arms and land-based equipment such as armoured vehicles, trucks and artillery.
Now, it is selling them more specialised weapons, including armed drones and electronic warfare systems.
Analysts noted that China’s African arms sales were shifting qualitatively to air-defence systems, armed drones and electronic warfare gear once dominated by Russia and the West.
In April, four vehicles identified by defence analysis group Janes as...
title: From rifles to radar: China upgrades its African arms trade as Russia and the West retreat

author: Cui Jianchun
description:
The 2026 Global Governance Forum in Xiongan, Hebei province, wrapped up on October 25. Against a backdrop of acute strains on multilateralism and a widening global governance deficit, the forum galvanised a shared sense of urgency across the international community for reform and solidarity.
More than a century ago, Karl Marx noted that, “Philosophers have hitherto only interpreted the world in various ways; the point is to change it.” That insight strikes at the very heart of today’s global...
title: China’s global initiatives offer ray of hope in a turbulent world

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Beijing has stepped up its maritime presence around Taiwan, deploying coastguard patrols from the island’s eastern approaches to waters near Quemoy and remote Dongsha Island.
Chinese coastguard spokesman Jiang Lue said on Saturday that a formation led by the vessel Hushi carried out routine law enforcement patrols east of Taiwan to reinforce administrative control and safeguard maritime navigation.
“Since October, the Hushi task group has been strengthening control over the relevant waters to...
title: Beijing ramps up maritime patrols around Taiwan, prompting Taipei to shadow ships

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taipei Mayor Wayne Chiang Wan-an faces an unexpectedly tough re-election fight in a race closely watched for its potential to damage the main opposition party Kuomintang and further strain the island’s relations with Beijing.
Just five months ago, Chiang appeared comfortably positioned for a second term in a city where the KMT has traditionally enjoyed an advantage over the ruling Democratic Progressive Party.
A poll by local cable news network TVBS in late May put him 28 percentage points ahead...
title: Could Taipei’s unexpectedly tight mayoral race add to cross-strait tensions?

author: Dulue Mbachu
description:
Russia’s influence has surged among young people across Africa in recent years, leaping over former colonial power France while still trailing China, a survey of African youths has found.
Many young Africans now perceive Russia to be an ally, observers said, warning its rivals to take the shift seriously as the continent becomes increasingly critical to both Moscow and Beijing.
According to the African Youth Survey commissioned by the South Africa-based Ichikowitz Family Foundation, 54 per cent...
title: Russia surpasses France in African youth appeal, still trails China: survey
